title: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies - National Values Education - Human Trafficking
exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
subject: National Values Education

questions.q: What is the best definition of Human Trafficking?
options: The legal migration of people from rural areas to cities for better jobs
The illegal trade of human beings for the purposes of exploitation, forced labour, or commercial sexual exploitation
The process of moving farm produce across international borders
The authorized adoption of children by wealthy families
questions.explain: **Human Trafficking** is a crime involving the illegal recruitment, transportation, or holding of persons by force, fraud, or deception, with the aim of exploiting them for profit.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which two demographic groups are statistically the most vulnerable and frequently targeted victims of human trafficking in Nigeria?
options: Adult men and elderly citizens
Politicians and civil servants
Women and children
University lecturers and doctors
questions.explain: Due to socio-economic vulnerabilities, physical disadvantage, and demand for domestic and sexual exploitation, **women and children** are disproportionately the primary targets of traffickers.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following is a major 'push factor' responsible for the high rate of children and women trafficking?
options: Abundance of high-paying jobs in the rural areas
Extreme poverty and desperation for survival
High quality of the public education system
Adequate national security checks
questions.explain: **Extreme poverty** is a primary driver. Traffickers prey on impoverished families by making false promises of good jobs or better lives abroad for their children.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When thousands of young, energetic youths are trafficked out of the country every year, the country directly suffers from:
options: An increase in national foreign reserve wealth
A loss of vibrant human resources and productive workforce
An immediate decrease in environmental pollution
Enhanced technological development
questions.explain: A severe macroeconomic consequence of human trafficking is the **loss of human resources**. The country is deprived of its young, potentially productive workforce.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Victims of human trafficking are frequently forced against their will into which of the following negative lifestyles?
options: A life of high academic scholarship and honors
A life of political leadership and civic duty
A life of crime, drug addiction, and sexual violence
A highly paid professional corporate job
questions.explain: Trafficked persons often endure brutal conditions and are forced into prostitution, begging, or drug couriering, exposing them to a **life of crime, addiction, and sexual violence**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: How does human trafficking typically impact the family structure of the victims?
options: It strengthens family love and unity across borders
It weakens family love, influence, and causes severe psychological trauma
It results in the immediate financial prosperity of the entire extended family
It legally forces the trafficker to become an adopted member of the victim's family
questions.explain: The sudden disappearance, death, or rescue of a traumatized victim shatters families, causing deep mistrust and trauma which severely **weakens family love and influence**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Aside from poverty, what other psychological factor largely allows traffickers to succeed in luring victims away from their homes?
options: Greed and Ignorance (believing deceitful promises)
High level of formal education
Extreme patriotism and national pride
Contentment with rural living
questions.explain: **Ignorance** about the realities of human trafficking and **greed** (a desire for rapid, unearned wealth) make individuals susceptible to the deceptive promises of traffickers.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which specific fundamental human right is completely denied to a victim of human trafficking?
options: The right to vote in local government elections
The right to freedom of speech on the internet
The right to personal liberty and freedom from slavery
The right to bear firearms
questions.explain: Human trafficking strips individuals of their fundamental **right to personal liberty**, dignity, and freedom from forced labour or slavery, turning humans into property.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Apart from poverty, which of the following is a major social factor responsible for the high rate of children and women trafficking?
options: High minimum wage in the victim's country
The desire to acquire advanced medical degrees
Deception and false promises of a better life abroad by relatives or strangers
Excessive involvement in communal labour
questions.explain: Traffickers frequently exploit the trust of vulnerable individuals through **deception**, making false promises of lucrative jobs, marriage, or better education abroad.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When trafficked individuals are subjected to sexual exploitation and forced prostitution, they are highly exposed to which of the following direct health consequences?
options: Improvement in psychological fitness
Contracting sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and HIV/AIDS
Developing resistance to common tropical diseases
Curing genetic disorders
questions.explain: A life of sexual violence and exploitation inevitably exposes victims to severe health hazards, primarily the high risk of **contracting STIs and HIV/AIDS**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following describes how human trafficking negatively impacts the national economy of the victim's home country?
options: It leads to the continuous drain of vibrant, young human resources
It forces foreign investors to build more local schools
It automatically increases the nation's foreign exchange reserves
It results in overpopulation in rural agricultural sectors
questions.explain: The economy suffers immensely due to the **loss of human resources**, as active youths who could have contributed to national productivity and development are taken away.
